method.scope: Prospective audit of the D0 input contract in the tagged v0.2.0 UI and exports
limitations: Persona satisfaction is a task-completion proxy, not measured user sentiment.
The audit distinguishes input semantics; it does not infer a production process model from rounded yield examples.

evidence: The tagged application immediately reports Gross 767, Yield 92.36%, and Expected Good approximately 708.
The visible field supplied a unit but did not say whether D0 must already represent the full process.
Neither the UI nor report stated that a baseline or per-mask D0 needing a separate process-complexity factor was unsupported.
The negative-binomial disclosure correctly described alpha as a defect-clustering parameter rather than process complexity.
JSON preserved the numeric defect-density input but had no metadata defining its process basis, and the visual report only said Defect density.
The four random-defect formulas and active-area exposure calculation were already explicit and numerically consistent.

personas.label: Keyboard user on a constrained viewport

evidence: The D0 field was reachable in the essentials section on a narrow viewport.
No always-visible policy text distinguished a usable full-process value from an incompatible baseline value.
The independent baseline remains Gross 767, Murphy yield 0.92360878014683934, and exact expected good 708.4079343726257.
The same number could be entered under materially different baseline, per-mask, or effective full-process interpretations without an on-screen warning.
The existing alpha parameter was defined only as clustering and was not silently reused as a mask or process-complexity factor.

findings.summary: The defect-density input basis was not auditable
evidence: A plausible baseline or per-mask value could be accepted by every built-in model and produce a precise but semantically invalid yield estimate.
